messages:
sam: quick question — adding a small progress badge in Console for long-running recomputes (telemetry aggregates). also: should low-priority recomputes be preemptible on Dedicated pools?

maria: +1 on the badge. we get lots of PMs asking 'is it still running' when it actually stalled. simple percent + ETA is fine. :eyes:

priya: preemptible on Dedicated is tricky. customers pay for reserved throughput — we can only preempt on spare capacity or on burst nodes, otherwise violates SLA. but for 'background' recomputes on shared slots maybe ok.

devin: technical tradeoff: preemption that evicts GPU memory will kill KV cache and increases cost to warm up. we should have a mode: 
- preemptible=true -> checkpoint + resumeable jobs (preferred)
- preemptible=evict -> immediate kill

sam: agree resumeable is the friendly option. UX question: expose as toggle in Console when scheduling recompute? or only via API/CLI?

maria: expose in Console but greyed out with tooltip if the target pool is Dedicated and SLA bound. tooltip text: "This project has reserved Dedicated capacity. Turning on preemption may migrate work to burst nodes."

priya: we also need server-side validation: API should reject preemptible=true for tenant with reserved_commitment unless they opt into "allow_background_preemptions" flag.

devin: implementation plan: (1) API flag + validation; (2) scheduler: prefer eviction by pausing job at checkpoint boundary; (3) console: badge + toggle + small help copy.

sam: can someone draft the console copy? short. my draft: "Background recompute — may be paused to prioritize live traffic. Progress updates shown below."

maria: maybe add ETA hint: "Progress updates shown below. ETA is best-effort."

priya: note on quotas: we should count paused time against quota or not? if we charge token-time while paused that feels wrong. propose: bill only for active compute time; paused time not charged.

devin: scheduler would need to persist checkpoints and only consume slots when active. doable but we need accounting signals. ops-bot: created issue RI-1427 to track scheduler + billing changes: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-1427

sam: nice. for the badge itself, do we want a streaming log link or a tiny expandable panel with last 5 events?

maria: expandable panel with last 5 events + link to full job log is best. keep badge compact.

priya: one more safety: canary the preemption path on Hosted (non-Dedicated) first — lower blast radius. we can flip console toggle for internal projects only in the first rollout.

devin: deployment checklist: 
```
- feature flag: recompute-preemptible-v1
- API validation hook
- scheduler checkpoint/resume logic
- console badge + toggle (internal-only rollout)
- billing: mark paused time as not billable
```

sam: timeline? can we aim for a dry-run in 2 weeks?

maria: I'll take console copy + placeholder UI. estimate 3 days.

priya: I'll own API validation and quota doc changes. estimate 4 days.

devin: I'll prototype resumeable checkpointing and scheduler changes. 1 week.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started run ri-recompute-checker on staging at 2026-03-19T15:03:20Z — job id staging-7723. logs: "checkpoint created, paused for 30s, resumed"

sam: great. can we add a small metric: recompute.pause_count and recompute.resume_latency? want to monitor pause/resume thrash.

priya: added metric to the RFC checklist.

maria: UI note — add small :hourglass: icon when paused. keeps folks from pinging SREs.

devin: one operational caveat — resume latency depends on KV cache hit rate. we'll need a pre-warm path for hot keys for fast resume. added to RI-1427 subtasks.

sam: ok team — thanks. next steps: maria/priya/devin sync tomorrow 10am PT and I'll draft rollout announcement for customers. :thumbsup:
